1.1: This the message from the Lord that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, grandson of Gedaliah, great-grandson of Amariah, and great-great-grandson of Hezekiah, back when Josiah son of Amon was king in Judah.
1.2: The Lord said, "I'ma wipe everything off the face of the earth."
1.3: "People, animals, birds in the sky, fish in the sea—gone. I'ma clean house. Anybody wildin' out or doing wicked stuff? They gettin' cut off too."
1.4: "I'ma stretch My hand out over Judah and everybody living in Jerusalem. All that Baal worship? Dead. I'ma erase every last trace of those fake gods and the priests that reppin' them."
1.5: "That includes folks who worship the stars up on the roof, folks who swear by Me and Milcom like they can play both sides."
1.6: "And the ones who walked away from Me, who don't seek Me or even try to check in? Yeah, them too."
1.7: Shhh… be quiet in the presence of the Lord God. The day of the Lord comin' real soon. He already got the sacrifice set and invited the guests.
1.8: "And when that day hits, I'm comin' for the big dogs too—the royal fam, the officials, the rich folks stuntin' in them foreign fits."
1.9: "Same day, I'ma deal with folks who step over the threshold like they above it all, stackin' up violence and lies in their homes."
1.10: The Lord says, "That day, you gon' hear folks crying at the Fish Gate, wailing in the Second Quarter, and loud crashes echoin' from the hills."
1.11: Y'all in Maktesh? Mourn hard. All them merchants gon' be wiped out. Money handlers? Done for.
1.12: "That day, I'ma pull up with lamps and search every corner of Jerusalem. I'ma punish them chillin' in complacency, the ones sayin' in they heart, 'God ain't gon' do nothin'—not good or bad.'"
1.13: "But they gon' lose everything. All they goods? Gone. Houses? Empty. They gon' build, but never live in it. Plant vineyards, but never sip that wine."
1.14: The great day of the Lord? It's close. Real close. Coming fast. It's gon' be loud, bitter, and full of chaos. Even the strongest gon' cry.
1.15: That day gon' be all wrath, pain, destruction, darkness, and despair. A whole cloud of gloom hangin' over the land.
1.16: Trumpets blowin', alarms ringin'. Fortified cities and high towers? Under attack.
1.17: "I'ma make folks stumble like blind men, 'cause they been sinning heavy. Blood gon' spill like dust. Bodies thrown out like trash."
1.18: Don't think your silver or gold can save you. On the day of God's wrath, all of it gettin' burned up. The whole land gon' feel the heat of His jealousy. He cleanin' house, quick and final.

2.1: Y'all better get it together—yes, all of y'all, you hard-headed nation.
2.2: Do it before God's decree drop. Before the time pass like dust in the wind. Before the Lord's anger pull up on y'all. Don't wait 'til the Day of the Lord's wrath hit!
2.3: All y'all humble folks out here that still try to do right—seek the Lord. Chase righteousness. Walk in humility. Maybe, just maybe, He'll hide you when that judgment hits.
2.4: Gaza gon' be abandoned. Ashkelon left in ruins. Ashdod getting run out in broad daylight. And Ekron? Ripped up from the roots.
2.5: Woe to y'all living by the coast—y'all Cherethites! The Lord got smoke for you. Canaan, land of the Philistines? You gettin' wiped clean. No one gon' be left.
2.6: That whole coast finna be empty pastures now. Just grass, shepherds, and sheep pens.
2.7: The leftovers from Judah? They gon' move in. They gon' feed they flocks out there. They gon' sleep in Ashkelon like it's theirs—because the Lord gon' come through for them and bring His people back.
2.8: "I been heard what Moab and Ammon been sayin'. All that trash talk, the way they've been wildin' against My people, threatening borders like they runnin' things."
2.9: "So as sure as I live," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "Moab gon' end up like Sodom. Ammon? Just like Gomorrah. Overrun with weeds, full of salt pits, and nothin' but wasteland."
2.10: "And guess what? My people, the ones who still standing? They takin' all that over. They gon' own it."
2.11: They brought that on themselves with all that pride, runnin' they mouth against God's people and actin' brand new.
2.12: But the Lord gon' make it known—He ain't to be played with. He gon' snatch every fake god off the map. Folks all over the world, from every coast, they gon' bow to Him from wherever they at.
2.13: "And you too, Ethiopians? My sword comin' for y'all too."
2.14: He gon' stretch His hand up north, destroy Assyria, and turn Nineveh into a dried-up ghost town—lookin' like a desert.
2.15: Animals gon' chill there like it's a field. All kinds of creatures—birds, wild beasts, you name it. Birds squawkin' through the windows. Ruins at the doorstep. He gon' tear all that fine cedar down.
2.16: This that city that used to be loud and proud, sittin' back comfy like, "I'm that girl—ain't nobody touchin' me." But look at her now—nothing but ruins. Just a rest stop for stray animals. Folks gon' pass by and hiss, throwin' shade and side-eyes.

3.1: Woe to that city that don't listen, that's full of mess and always tryna hurt folks.
3.2: She don't listen to God's voice. Won't take no correction. Ain't even tryin' to trust the Lord or get close to Him.
3.3: Her leaders? Like lions, loud and always lookin' to devour. Her judges? Like wolves that leave nothin' behind—not even bones by the next morning.
3.4: Her prophets out here wildin', actin' reckless and fake. The priests done messed up the temple and broke God's law like it ain't nothin'.
3.5: But the Lord? He still righteous right there in the city. He don't do no wrong. Every morning He bring justice like clockwork. He don't miss. But the wicked? They don't even feel shame.
3.6: "I done tore down nations," God says. "Left their cities empty. Ain't nobody walkin' them streets. They ruined, straight deserted."
3.7: "I thought for sure y'all would finally respect Me after all that. Thought y'all would learn something so I wouldn't have to destroy your home. But nah—they woke up early just to keep doin' wrong."
3.8: "So wait on Me," says the Lord. "When I rise up to get what's Mine, I'm bringin' all nations together for judgment. I'm pourin' out My fierce anger. The whole earth gettin' dealt with."
3.9: "But after that, I'mma clean up the people's speech—make it pure—so everybody can call on My name and serve Me side by side."
3.10: "From way beyond Ethiopia, My people gon' come back and worship Me again. They bringin' Me offerings with love."
3.11: "On that day, you won't be ashamed for how you acted before. I'mma get rid of the proud ones who always actin' superior. You ain't gon' be stuntin' on My holy mountain no more."
3.12: "I'ma leave behind a humble, quiet people—folk who lean fully on the name of the Lord."
3.13: "That remnant? They won't lie. Won't do folks dirty. No slick talk. They gon' rest easy, feed they flocks, and sleep in peace—with no fear."
3.14: Sing loud, daughter Zion! Shout up, Israel! Be glad and go 'head and rejoice with everything you got!
3.15: The Lord done cleared your record. He kicked the enemy out. Your King—yeah, the Lord—He right there with you. No more disaster, period.
3.16: On that day, people gon' say to Jerusalem: "Don't trip! Don't be scared! Don't let your hands hang down in fear."
3.17: The Lord your God is with you, strong and mighty to save. He delights in you. He gon' calm you down with His love and sing over you with joy.
3.18: "I'ma gather all the ones who hurt from missing out on worship, the ones who been feelin' heavy 'cause of the shame they carry."
3.19: "At that time, I'mma handle everybody that did y'all dirty. I'll heal the hurt, bring back the ones who got pushed out, and give y'all a name and respect everywhere you used to get clowned."
3.20: "When I bring y'all back and gather y'all together again, I'mma make the whole world give y'all praise and honor. I'll restore everything right before your eyes," says the Lord.
